idea-plugin.description:
Navigation and inspections for Cucumber suites written in Java, resolved through a file index instead of a scan of every step definition in the project.

Navigation

  • Step to definition — Ctrl+click or Ctrl+B from any step in a feature file.
  • Definition to steps — a gutter icon and a 3 Gherkin steps hint above each step definition. Both open the same list, where every row names the scenario and the file and line it lives on, and moving over a row previews that whole scenario with the step marked.

Debugging

  • Breakpoints in feature files — click the gutter beside a step and the debugger stops at the top of its step definition, before the step does anything. It stops only while that step is running, not for every other step sharing the definition, and it needs no particular runner: JUnit, Gradle, Maven and remote attach all work.

Inspections

  • Undefined step, with a quick fix that writes the missing method — deriving {int}, {string} and {float} parameters from the step text and adding it to the class that already holds the most step definitions.
  • Unused step definition: one no feature file uses. Dead weight that accumulates as features are reworded, and that a passing test run never points out.
  • Ambiguous step: one that two definitions match. Cucumber fails these at runtime with AmbiguousStepDefinitionsException, while the IDE otherwise hides the problem by quietly resolving to whichever pattern is longest.

Editing

  • Step completion inside feature files, offered from the project's own step definitions and matched against the whole step text typed so far, not just the last word.
  • Parameter values highlighted inside each step.
  • Renaming a step rewrites the feature files and the step definition's pattern together.

What it recognises

  • Annotation step definitions and io.cucumber.java8 lambda ones.
  • Localized annotations such as io.cucumber.java.de.Angenommen, and localized feature files declaring # language: de.
  • Every built-in parameter type — {int}, {float}, {word}, {string}, {byte}, {short}, {long}, {double}, {biginteger}, {bigdecimal} and the anonymous {} — plus optional text (cuke(s)), alternation (cat/dog), and any @ParameterType the project declares.

Why it stays quick

Step definitions are found by a lexer pass over Java sources, with no parsing and no resolving, and bucketed by the leading literal words of their pattern. Resolving a step then compares it against the handful of definitions that could plausibly match, and touches PSI only once one does. Over a synthetic suite of 3,000 step definitions that resolves around 14 times faster than the equivalent linear pass, and it does not slow down as a suite grows.

Requirements

Needs the Gherkin plugin, which the IDE offers to install alongside this one. Running a scenario from the gutter is not provided here yet; Cucumber for Java still covers that, and the two can be installed together.

Built with AI assistance. The repository documents what is covered by tests and what is known to be missing.
